# claude.md - Register Errands - Dynamic (tree 518765124)

## Purpose
ETG (eTraveli Group) agent workflow, embedded in Zendesk. For a cancellation contact, the agent looks up the Edvin order, selects PNRs/passengers/channel/type, picks a customer action per PNR, and the tree auto-creates the Zendesk child/silent/grandchild tickets, registers the errand in Edvin, and posts an internal note.

## Architecture (flow) - REWRITTEN FOR v46, 2026-09-02

Everything below is verified against this export's actual node ids. The three
DRIFT/CORRECTION notes that used to live here are gone: they described node
numbers from v26/v37/v42 that have not existed for several versions, and keeping
them meant every reader had to work out which half of the section to believe.
Anything earlier than v45 in the Changelog is history, not a map.

Root = 10 (Clear session and start fresh order).

INTAKE
  10 -> 77 Verify Order Reference -> 4 Edvin Find Order -> 13 status
  13 -> 61 Insert Linked PNRs -> 6 Select PNRs -> 24 Set order context & channel
  24 -> 54 PNR selection made? -> [55 re-pick] | 75 Is VI selection? -> [76 VI subtree] | 7
  7 Set Selected PNRs -> 8 Select Passengers -> 9 Format Passengers -> 56 selection made?
  56 -> [57 re-pick] | 42 GET Edvin Errands -> 26 status -> 46 Format Types -> 1 Select
  Channel & Type -> 2 Build actions_array + push PNR -> 11 More PNRs? -> loop to 7, else 12
  12 Create PNR Action Table -> 25 Display table -> 58 Check selections -> 59 all picked?
  59 -> [60 re-pick] | 27

GROUPING
  27 Stitch & Group -> builds transforms.work_queue + transforms.final_pnrs -> 3

TICKET LOOP (ONE loop, child + silent + grand child - v45)
  3 Any tickets to create? -> [none: 21] | 32
  32 Loop Tickets (cursor) -> 84 Validate Ticket Data -> 33 Create Ticket (CO #20) -> 17 status
  17 -> 62 Updating Tickets -> 64 Set Side Conversation Id -> 63 Get Ticket Details (CO #158)
  39 status -> 65 Resolve Ticket Id -> 66 Update Ticket (CO #207) -> 41 status -> 34
  34 Is More Tickets? -> loop to 32, else 21

ERRAND LOOP
  21 Format Internal Note -> 22 Add Internal Note (CO #57) -> 15 status
  15 -> 44 Loop Errands to Register (cursor) -> 78 Validate Errand Details
     -> 43 Register Errand (CO #160) -> 30 status
  30 -> 83 Is More PNRs? -> loop to 44, else 89

CLOSE
  89 Render Execution Log -> 23 Closing Call
  23 -> [47 Additional/Different Request -> 29 Clear Data -> 77] | [48 End Session]
  48 End Session prints ${transforms.execution_log_html} - the run's read-out lands
  at the end of the session, not on the Closing Call.

FAILURE (shared - v45)
  Every status check's failure branch (13, 15, 17, 26, 30, 39, 41) -> 86 API Failure -
  Log & Render -> 87 Request Failed -> [Retry: 88 Retry Router -> the Data node that
  failed, chosen by last_api_alias] | [End Session: 53]

## Data dictionary

### v46 (2026-09-02) - the entries that supersede everything below them

- transforms.work_queue - THE structure the ticket loop walks. Built by node 27,
  consumed by node 32. One entry per Zendesk ticket, grand children nested inside:
      [ { ticket: { kind, title, pnr, bucket, category, contact_reason,
                    customer_action, type, channel, genesys_interaction_type,
                    errand_key, status, passengers,
                    grand_child_tickets: [ { ...same shape... } ] },
          errands: [ { ...the final_pnrs record(s) this ticket covers... } ] } ]
  kind is child | silent | grand_child. status is open | solved and is what node 65
  sends to the Zendesk update - node 65 no longer sniffs the title for "Silent".
  errand_key is type + "|" + customer_action, the same key node 27/44 group on, and
  the join back to final_pnrs. The errands arrays hold REFERENCES to the same
  records final_pnrs holds, not copies - node 44 still reads final_pnrs and is
  unchanged. REPLACES transforms.child_tickets, which no longer exists.
- Loop cursors (FORM data, no TTL): queue_index (which work_queue entry) and
  grandchild_index (-1 = the parent ticket itself, 0..n-1 = that grand child).
  Both are reset to 0 / -1 by node 27 on every pass, and clamp on entry in node 32.
  current_queue_index / current_is_grand_child are the position node 32 just
  PROCESSED - node 65 needs those, because by the time it runs the cursor has moved.
  is_more_tickets is node 34's routing boolean. REPLACES child_tickets_count,
  grandchild_tickets_count, is_more_child_tickets, is_grandchild_tickets and
  is_more_grandchild_tickets, all of which are gone.
- transforms.resolved_ticket_ids_by_queue_index - { queue_index: zendesk_ticket_id },
  written by node 65 for parent tickets only. A grand child reads its own parent's
  entry to fill target_ticket_id. REPLACES transforms.resolved_child_ticket_id,
  which only ever held "the last one resolved" and worked by luck of adjacency.
- transforms.current_ticket - the ticket being processed this pass, parent or grand
  child. REPLACES current_child_ticket and current_grandchild_ticket.
- transforms.ticket_card_html - node 84's agent card (was child_ticket_html).
  ticket_kind / ticket_display_index / tickets_total (FORM) drive its heading.
- transforms.child_ticket - UNCHANGED NAME ON PURPOSE. CO #20's request body reads
  ${transforms.child_ticket.*} and lives in the admin UI, not in this export, so
  renaming it here would break the create call silently. It is the Zendesk payload
  { subject, body, orderReference, target_ticket_id }, not a ticket record.
- GONE, DELIBERATELY (v46, Brent): attempted_child_ticket_keys,
  attempted_grandchild_ticket_keys, created_child_ticket_keys,
  created_grandchild_ticket_keys, registered_errand_keys, and the
  ticket_already_created / skip_errand_registration flags. See "THIS TREE IS AN ETL"
  under Conventions before reintroducing any of them.
- execution_log (FORM data) - see "EXECUTION LOG" under Conventions.
  Companions: execution_log_seq, pending_api_node/step/alias/ref, last_api_alias,
  transforms.execution_log_html, transforms.failure_html.

- transforms.channel / transforms.category: full Edvin errand-config OBJECTS {id,name,categories}. Set in node 46. Store only .name on PNR items (see node 2).
- transforms.customer_action_pnrs: array of PNR items {pnr, channel(name), channelId, category(name), categoryId, type, typeId, notes, actions_array}. Built in node 2, restitched in node 27.
- actions_array item: {id, name, bucket(STRING), actionId, ...}. bucket normalized to a string in node 2 (bucketKey).
- transforms.child_tickets: [{child_ticket:{...grandchild_tickets:[]}}]. Built node 27 by grouping stitched PNRs on the DISTINCT (type+action) key: proceed -> ONE active child (grandchildren = one per distinct type+action, only when 2+ combos); non-proceed -> ONE silent ticket per distinct (type+action). Consumed node 32 loop.
- transforms.child_ticket_html (v41, undocumented until now): the agent-facing card
  rendered by node 84 (Content, `${transforms.child_ticket_html}`). Built in node 32
  by buildErrandCardHtml(), which reads .title/.pnr/.bucket/.customer_action/.type/
  .formatted_passengers/.passengers off its payload argument - that shape belongs to
  transforms.current_child_ticket (= child_tickets[cursor].child_ticket, set earlier
  in node 32), NOT the local `child_ticket` object node 32 also builds a few lines
  later for node 33's Zendesk create call (subject/body/orderReference/target_ticket_id
  only - no pnr/passengers). Passing the wrong one is exactly what produced a blank
  "PNR " title and "No passenger details available" on every card - see changelog.
- transforms.final_pnrs: one entry per distinct (type+action). Built node 27 (deduped), consumed ONLY by node 44 (registers one Edvin errand each). v19: node 21 no longer reads it - the internal note reads transforms.customer_action_pnrs so every PNR appears, even when two PNRs share the same type AND action (ZD 7621694). FIXED 2026-08-21 (ZD 337619): each final_pnrs entry used to spread group[0] alone, so an errand covering 2+ PNRs silently dropped every PNR after the first from the Edvin message. buildFinalErrandRecord() (node 27) now combines the whole group - pnr becomes the joined PNR list (joinPnrs), passengers/formatted_passengers are unioned and de-duped, orderReference is the de-duped set joined - before node 44 formats it. FIXED 2026-08-21's pass missed .notes - it stayed on the group[0] spread, so a second PNR's agent notes were dropped from the Edvin "Agent Notes" line whenever 2+ PNRs collapsed into one errand. FIXED 2026-08-24: mergeNotes(group) now builds notes as "PNR: note | PNR: note" (non-empty, de-duped) before node 44 formats it. See changelog.
- transforms.unresolved_selections: [{pnr, field, raw, reason, reason_text, bucket, type}] - every PNR whose selection could not be turned into (action + known bucket). Built node 27, rendered by node 27 into transforms.unresolved_note_html for node 51, counted by node 21's log.
- has_unresolved_selections / unresolved_selections_count (FORM data): node 50's routing boolean and its count. Form data because logic-node expressions read scalars by name.
- transforms.attempted_child_ticket_keys / attempted_grandchild_ticket_keys (v35):
  the titles this session has ATTEMPTED to create. Recorded by nodes 32 and 36 BEFORE
  the create fires; read by those same nodes as the duplicate guard that nodes 13/15
  route on. These - not the created_* lists - are what stop a duplicate ticket.
- transforms.created_child_ticket_keys / created_grandchild_ticket_keys: titles Zendesk
  CONFIRMED (nodes 14/16, 2xx only). RECONCILIATION INPUT ONLY since v35 - node 21
  compares them against planned_ticket_titles to warn about a ticket it cannot prove
  exists. Do not route a duplicate guard off these again; see Conventions.
- transforms.registered_errand_keys (v35): one entry per (type|customer_action) already
  sent to Edvin this session. Recorded by node 44 before node 43 fires; node 17 routes
  on it. Deliberately NOT cleared by node 27, so a Back-nav replay cannot re-register an
  errand Edvin already holds, while a selection the agent genuinely changed makes a new
  key and registers normally.
- skip_errand_registration (FORM data, v35): node 17's routing boolean. True when this
  errand's key is already registered, or when the cursor has no item at all.
- transforms.planned_ticket_titles: every child/silent/grandchild title this run intends to create. Built node 27, compared in node 21 against created_child_ticket_keys + created_grandchild_ticket_keys so the note cannot promise a ticket Zendesk never confirmed.
- grandchild_parent_resolved / grandchild_parent_blocked (FORM data, v36, restructured
  v37): routing booleans set by whichever check node in the resolve chain last ran
  (18, 28, or 55) and tested by that attempt's router (19, 30, or 56). resolved=true
  means targetTicketId was proven this pass (grandchild_parent_id now holds it);
  blocked=true is set ONLY by node 55, the final attempt, when resolution never
  happened across all 3 tries. Mutually exclusive by construction; reset per child
  ticket by node 39, and by nodes 10/29 between sessions.
  v37 DROPPED child_ticket_resolve_attempts (v36's poll counter) - which attempt is
  running is now which node you are at (18=1st, 28=2nd, 55=3rd/final), not runtime
  state. See Conventions "GRANDCHILD-PARENT RESOLVE CHAIN" for why.
- transforms.blocked_grandchild_parent_keys / blocked_grandchild_ticket_titles (v36):
  written by node 55 (the final resolve-chain attempt) only when all 3 tries came up
  empty. The first is the child ticket's title (for diagnostics); the second is every
  grandchild title under it that was NEVER attempted (not pushed to
  attempted_grandchild_ticket_keys, since node 36 never ran for them). Node 21 prints
  these as a distinct BLOCKED line, and excludes them from the generic "not confirmed"
  reconciliation warning so the two states are never conflated. Reset by nodes 10/29.
- Counters: child_tickets_count, grandchild_tickets_count (form data, no TTL) and
  transforms.final_pnrs_count (node 44). All three clamp on entry and reset to 0 when
  exhausted, so every loop is re-runnable - final_pnrs_count only since v35.
- Display counters (FORM data, v43): child_ticket_display_index/child_tickets_total (node 32, read by node 84's "Create Child Ticket X of Y" heading), grandchild_ticket_display_index/grandchild_tickets_total (node 36, node 85's heading), errand_display_index/final_pnrs_total (node 44, node 78's heading). Each is the 1-based position of the item about to be processed THIS pass (cursor value + 1, read before that cursor increments), paired with the loop's total length. Purely presentational - never read by logic nodes or Connected Objects; do not confuse with the *_count cursor variables above, which are 0-based and drive the loop itself.
- has_customer_action_selection (FORM data, v43, fixed 2026-08-27): node 58's routing boolean, gating new Scoring node 59 between node 25 and node 27. True only when EVERY row in transforms.customer_action_pnrs has a non-blank customer_action_<pnr>_<index> (originally .some() - any ONE row - which is the bug the 2026-08-27 correction entry fixed). transforms.missing_customer_action_pnrs (node 58) lists the PNRs still blank, rendered on node 60. Distinct from has_unresolved_selections (node 27, existing) - see the v43 section below.
- Counters (form data, no TTL): child_tickets_count, grandchild_tickets_count; booleans is_more_child_tickets, is_grandchild_tickets, is_more_grandchild_tickets, is_more_pnrs, isMorePNR.
- actions.edvin__errand_configuration, actions.get_edvin_prop_long_value: Edvin API responses.

## External systems (CX Actions / Connected Objects)
Edvin: Find Order (4), GET Edvin Errands (42), Register Errand (43). Zendesk: Update Tags (31), Create Child Ticket (33), Create Grandchild Ticket (37), Get Side Conversations (40), Add Internal Note (22).

## Conventions & gotchas

- EXECUTION LOG (v46). Every API call this tree makes writes one line to the
  `execution_log` FORM variable - form data, so it outlives the 1-hour transforms
  TTL and a deep resume. It is a flat string with two delimiters so a parser needs
  exactly two split() calls:
      entries  split on  ~||~
      fields   split on  ~:~   ->  seq, ts, node, step, status, code, ref, detail
  status is OK | FAIL | SKIP | INFO. Anything a value could contain that looks like
  a delimiter is neutralised by logClean() (tildes become hyphens, newlines become
  spaces, 300-char cap per field). The whole string is capped at 20000 chars and
  trims WHOLE entries off the front, never a partial one.
  Mechanism, three functions, defined in a block that is byte-identical in every
  script that logs (nodes 9, 10, 21, 29, 32, 44, 46, 61, 64, 65, 86, 89):
      logArm(node, step, alias, ref)  the script immediately BEFORE a Data node
                                      names the call that is about to happen
      logFlush()                      first line of every script that can follow a
                                      Data node - grades the armed call off
                                      actions.<alias>._zt_meta and appends one entry
      logWrite(...)                   direct append, for SKIP and INFO lines
  A call is armed only when it is actually going to fire: node 32 and node 44 write
  a SKIP line instead of arming when their idempotency guard says the work is done,
  because arming a call that never fires would leave the PREVIOUS response under
  the same alias for the next script to grade as this one's success.
  Node 86 flushes the failure BEFORE the agent sees the retry screen and then
  re-arms the same call, so a request that failed once and succeeded on retry
  leaves both lines behind. That was the whole point of centralising the failure
  screen - the per-request screens could not do it.
  Node 89 renders the log grouped failures-first into transforms.execution_log_html
  (nodes 23 and 53 print it; node 86 prints it on the failure screen too).
  NOTHING ROUTES ON THE LOG. It is a read-out, not state.
  DUPLICATION IS DELIBERATE BUT NOT FREE: the block is copied into 12 scripts
  because Zingtree User Functions (ZT.<yourFunction>) are defined in the admin UI,
  not in a tree export, so a tree-only change cannot centralise it. If someone
  registers logArm/logFlush/logWrite as User Functions, every one of those blocks
  collapses to a single ZT.logFlush() line. Until then, a change to the block is a
  change to 12 nodes - the same drift hazard already documented for BUCKET_BY_ID
  in nodes 2 and 46.
  ZT.log() was removed tree-wide in the same pass (Brent, 2026-09-02): it wrote to
  Execution Insights, which is a separate store nobody was reading, and this log
  covers the same ground where it can actually be seen.

- UNIFIED TICKET LOOP (v46). Child, silent and grand child tickets all run through
  ONE loop body: 32 -> 84 -> 33 -> 17 -> 62 -> 64 -> 63 -> 39 -> 65 -> 66 ->
  41 -> 34. The old grandchild body (36, 37, 38, 68, 69, 70, 71, 72, 85 and status
  checks 19, 20, 49, 50, 51, 52, plus router 35) called the SAME three Connected
  Objects as the child body - #20 create, #158 get details, #207 update - so it was
  a verbatim clone whose only real difference was target_ticket_id. It is deleted.
  Node 32 walks work_queue depth-first: the parent ticket, then each of its grand
  children, then the next entry. That ORDER IS THE CONTRACT - a parent is always
  created and resolved before its grand children, which is the only reason a grand
  child can read its parent's id out of resolved_ticket_ids_by_queue_index.
  Do not reorder the walk without moving that lookup.
  PLATFORM RISK TO WATCH IN SANDBOX: node 32 is now re-entered once per TICKET
  rather than once per child ticket, so a run with a child plus three grand children
  hits it four times instead of one. Zingtree's engine flags repeated re-entry into
  the same node or short node cycle as an "invalid loop" independently of whether
  the counter logic is correct (Brent hit exactly this on v36 - see the v37
  resolve-chain entry). The loop passes through Content node 84 every pass, which is
  the paced-checkpoint shape that fixed it last time, but this is the one thing in
  v45 the offline harness cannot see. Test it live before promoting.

- THIS TREE IS AN ETL, AND API ERROR HANDLING IS THE SAFEGUARD (v46, Brent's call,
  2026-09-02). Load the order from Edvin, let the agent pick PNRs / passengers /
  type / customer actions, build one data structure from those picks, then fire the
  sequence programmatically: create ticket -> get details -> update -> grand
  children if any -> next ticket -> internal note -> register errands -> close.
  There is NO "have I already created this?" check anywhere, by design.
  History, so nobody re-derives it: v44 and everything before it CARRIED such
  guards - attempted_child_ticket_keys, created_*_keys, registered_errand_keys, and
  the ticket_already_created / skip_errand_registration flags - but no node ever
  routed on them. They had been dead code since the v42 renumbering broke the node
  ids the older claude.md entries name ("node 13/15", "node 45"). v45 wired them up
  as nodes 90/91; Brent removed both the same day. The guards were state that
  pretended to be a safety net, and a replay they suppressed silently was worse to
  debug than one that shows up in the log.
  What actually protects a run now: every API call is status-checked, every failure
  routes to the shared failure screen (86/87/88), and every call - success, failure
  and retry - is written to the execution log. A Back-nav replay of node 27 DOES
  re-run the ETL and DOES create a second set of tickets. That is accepted, and it
  is visible: walk_v46.mjs's "replay node 27" scenario asserts exactly that, and
  asserts the log contains all six creates with no SKIP lines hiding any of them.
  If duplicates ever become a real operational problem, the fix is upstream - stop
  node 25's Back from re-entering node 27 - not a key list inside the loop.

- SHARED FAILURE SCREEN (v46). Nodes 14, 16, 18, 28, 31, 40 and 45 - seven
  near-identical "Request Failed" content nodes - are replaced by 86 (script: log
  the failure, build the screen) -> 87 (content) -> 88 (retry router). 88 branches
  on last_api_alias, a form variable logArm() sets and never clears, back to the
  Data node that failed. ADDING A NEW API CALL MEANS ADDING A BUTTON TO NODE 88.
  If you forget, its Retry falls through node 88's default straight to node 53
  (Session Ended) - the run ends safely, but the agent cannot retry.

- A DUPLICATE GUARD MUST RECORD THE ATTEMPT, NOT THE CONFIRMATION (v35, learned from
  ZD 334818). v25 made nodes 14/16 record a title only on a confirmed 2xx, so that a
  failed create would still be retried and flagged. But the guards read those same
  lists - so a create Zendesk actually MADE and reported badly stayed unrecorded, and
  the next pass created a second ticket. The two jobs need two lists: attempted_* for
  the guard (written before the call), created_* for the note's warning (written after).
  When in doubt, prefer a note that says "not confirmed - check the ticket list" over a
  duplicate written against a customer's order.
- EVERY CURSOR LOOP CLAMPS ON ENTRY AND RESETS ON EXHAUSTION. Node 44 was the one loop
  missing both, so after a full pass its cursor sat at final_pnrs.length and a replay
  read final_pnrs[out-of-range] === undefined - registering a REAL Edvin errand with no
  type, action or PNR. Nodes 32 and 36 are the reference shape.
- This tree is RE-ENTERED ROUTINELY. Node 25 has Back enabled and keep_vars_on_back=1,
  so Back + Continue re-fires node 27 and everything downstream of it. Any node that
  writes to Zendesk or Edvin must be idempotent under that replay - test it, don't
  assume it. walk.mjs (Workflow JSONs/ETG/) walks the real continuation graph and counts
  the actual create calls; the offline harness stubs them and cannot see this class of
  bug.
- Transforms expire after 1 hour; node 29 Clear Data resets loop state so the outer "Additional request" loop restarts clean.
- Node 3 guard (len(transforms.child_tickets) >= 1) MUST stay before node 32 — node 32->33 creates a Zendesk ticket unconditionally, so an empty set has to skip to 21.
- BUCKET LABELS vs ROUTING KEYS (v31/v32 - the cause of "bucket is not one Zingtree
  routes on"). Edvin returns the bucket as an OBJECT {id, name} where `name` is a HUMAN
  LABEL, not the snake_case key this tree branches on. bucketKey() only extracted that
  label, so node 27 - which trims and lowercases before testing KNOWN_BUCKETS - accepted
  "Proceed" (it happens to lowercase into the key) and rejected everything else.
  VERIFIED against the live errand-configuration response (2026-08-04). Across all three
  channels and all thirteen categories Edvin uses exactly THREE buckets, ids stable:
      id 3  "No action"          -> no_action
      id 4  "Proceed"            -> proceed
      id 5  "Different request"  -> different_request
  There is NO "escalate" bucket in Edvin. KNOWN_BUCKETS still lists it; that is harmless
  (it never occurs) - do not invent a mapping for it.
  Measured on the real Cancellation category (17 types, 137 action slots): the pre-fix
  build rejected 88 of 137 - every No action and every Different request. v32 routes all
  137, split proceed 49 / no_action 75 / different_request 13.
  v32 MATCHES ON THE BUCKET ID FIRST (BUCKET_BY_ID). The id is the contract; the label is
  display text ETG can reword at any time, and a reworded label silently breaks a
  name-only map. BUCKET_BY_NAME is the fallback for a bucket that arrives as a bare
  string. An unmapped bucket is returned UNCHANGED, never guessed - node 27 then flags it
  and stops the run, because guessing no_action for something that might mean Proceed
  records "the customer declined" against a customer who did not. Node 46 logs
  "edvin bucket labels seen: [...]" every session.
  KEEP THE BLOCK IDENTICAL IN NODES 2 AND 46 - both feed node 27; drift means the same
  action routes two different ways. Verified by realsweep.mjs against edvin_real.json.
- bucket routing keys: proceed | no_action | escalate | different_request. As of v24 an unrecognized or blank bucket is NO LONGER a default-to-silent-ticket; it is a problem that halts the run at node 50.
- UNUSABLE SELECTIONS NEVER GET RECORDED (v24, the rule that matters most here): a PNR that does not resolve to a real action with a known bucket must not become a ticket or an Edvin errand. "We could not read the selection" and "the customer declined" produce identical output otherwise, and only one of them is safe to write against an order. Node 27 classifies the problem (selection_unreadable | lookup_failed | bucket_missing | bucket_unrecognized), writes EMPTY child_tickets/final_pnrs, and sets has_unresolved_selections; node 50 routes to node 51, which sends the agent back to node 12 to re-pick. Do not "fix" this by restoring the old warning-in-the-note behaviour - the note used to apologize for a fact it had already recorded.
- NO <p> WRAPPER AROUND GENERATED HTML (v24): node 25 renders ${transforms.customer_action_table_html} bare, and node 51 renders ${transforms.unresolved_note_html} bare. The table HTML opens with a <style> block and <div>s; block-level content inside <p> makes the browser close the paragraph early and re-parent everything after it, which is the leading suspect for the <select> values that never reached node 27 (ZD 334703). It renders fine either way, so this is easy to reintroduce by accident.
- THE SUMMARY IS A PLAN, NOT A RECEIPT: node 27 computes the child/grandchild/silent counts before any create call fires. Node 21 reconciles them against the titles nodes 14/16 recorded and appends a warning for any gap. When verifying a run, open the tickets - do not trust the counts alone.
- GROUPING KEY (v11, restored for silent tickets in v33): distinct errand =
  (type + customer_action) TOGETHER, never action alone. ONE key governs everything:
    grandchildren   - one per distinct pair among PROCEED PNRs, only when 2+ pairs
    silent tickets  - one per distinct pair among NON-PROCEED PNRs (v33)
    Edvin errands   - one per distinct pair across ALL PNRs
  Scales to N: three non-proceed PNRs spanning three distinct pairs -> three silent
  tickets. v18 had consolidated non-proceed into a SINGLE silent ticket covering all of
  them; tracker "Testing 3" (2026-08-05) reverses that - Tests 5, 6a and 8 each expect 2
  silent, Test 6b expects 1. Do not re-consolidate without changing the tracker and the
  regression skill's oracle.js in the same edit; they encode this rule independently.
- ARCHITECTURE DECISION - GROUPING STAYS IN NODE 27, NOT NODE 44 (2026-08-21, Brent
  asked whether node 44 should own all errand formatting/grouping so it's isolated in
  one place). Decision: no - keep the split as-is. Node 27 computes "which PNRs make up
  which errand" ONCE, using the exact same (type + customer_action) key and the same
